smp_leg_unit.note: The one Leg of a Trial's Brief (kogaki#1664), rebuilt to the Leg with no Move (kogaki#1768). AUTHORED HERE, its point text COPIED from the Move-Extraction Playground's `leg_path_unit` row through `copies` (kogaki#1775).
smp_leg_unit.judgment_point: THE ARTICLE'S LANGUAGE (kogaki#1417): `language` in the input is the one language the article is written in, declared by the Audience file; write every proposition you compose in it, and keep in English only the keys and ids the record's shape fixes. compose ONE LEG for this Brief -- the Leg that builds the RelationalStructure in the input, `structure`, for the reader, opening from what the Persona already knows, rendered in the input as `persona_prior_knowledge` (kogaki#1664, kogaki#1699). A Leg carries no reader state (kogaki#1699) and binds no Move (kogaki#1768): the paragraph Move is bound per Brief Waypoint by /paragraph-plan, after the Brief (kogaki#1375). The Harness marks the last Leg `reaches_target` (kogaki#1532). EVERY LEG CARRIES ITS WAYPOINTS (kogaki#1311): the ordered route through the Leg, ONE BRIEF WAYPOINT PER ENTRY OF `claims` IN THE INPUT, IN ORDER (kogaki#1664). {{copy:point}} Brief Waypoint N is what the reader must come to hold for Claim N. THE WORDS ARE THE STRUCTURE'S (kogaki#1664): this Brief composes no renderings record; Claim N's `proposition` and Brief Waypoint N's `point` are written in the words of entry N's `material` -- a word that is in none of it and is not a function word is refused naming the word. Write the points from the structure's Role `context` and relation `holds` sentences, IN ORDER (kogaki#1664). EACH WAYPOINT RECORDS ITS `case` (kogaki#1732): `own` where its paragraph tells the subject's own case, `apart` where it tells a case apart from the subject, in material the reader already holds -- a record of what you decided when you wrote the waypoint, chosen from the Persona's prior knowledge; it adds no paragraph, and the waypoint after an `apart` one carries that case's structure onto the subject, so a Leg never ends on `apart`. THE STRUCTURE STANDS IN FOR STRANDS (kogaki#1664): Claim N is the `holds` sentence of entry N of `claims` in the input, addressed `L<N>` as its `claim_strand`, and its `proposition` is that sentence word for word; the Leg carries ONE Claim per entry, and Brief Waypoint N names in `serves` the Claim of entry N. Brief Waypoint N's `point` is written from entry N's `material`, the `context` of each Role and the `holds` of each relation the entry relates. The Leg carries exactly as many Brief Waypoints as `claims` has entries.
smp_leg_unit.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying `legs`, an array of EXACTLY ONE Leg, and nothing else. The Leg carries exactly these keys: `leg_id`; `claims` -- one `{ "type": "strand", "strand": "L<N>", "proposition": <entry N's holds, word for word> }` per entry of `claims` in the input, in order; and `waypoints` -- one `{ "point": <one sentence>, "serves": ["L<N>"], "case": "own" | "apart" }` per entry, in order. Every field means what src/leg-schema.json, rendered below, says it means. A Leg binds no Move (kogaki#1768), and the Harness writes nothing onto it.
smp_leg_unit.refusal: a key the record or the Leg does not declare, or a declared key missing; not exactly one Leg; a Claim whose `proposition` is not its entry's `holds`; and the Move-Extraction Playground's `validateLegPathUnit` over the Leg, imported, with each entry's `material` as the text its Claim and point are recovered from. Each refusal is put back into your next round verbatim.
smp_leg_unit.governing: the Move-Extraction Playground's `leg_path_unit` row and its point text; kogaki#1664; kogaki#1768; kogaki#1775

sme_map_roles.note: The Mapper's structure reading (kogaki#1665, kogaki#1721): one call reads the proposition into a RelationalStructure for the Persona. A second variant is a second row and a second Trial, never an edit of this one.
sme_map_roles.judgment_point: read the proposition in the input, `proposition`, as a relation among Roles. For each Role, define it in one or two sentences, as its `context`, as a kind of thing in the world of the Persona in `persona`: an abstraction the proposition's object is one instance of, never that object itself, written in the third person and naming no reader, writer or Persona. Name, as its `attributes`, the one-place predicates the proposition states of that Role's object, each one short phrase in the proposition's own words, or an empty list where it states none. Name each relation among Roles as the proposition states it, as its `holds`: one sentence stating the relation over the Roles, naming none of the proposition's objects and writing each Role it relates as `{<id>}`, that Role's id in braces, at least once, with `between` naming the Roles it relates. Name the one relation among those relations the proposition turns on, as `higher_order`, with `relates` naming the relations it relates and `holds` stating it over the same Roles, each written as `{<id>}`. Answer the RelationalStructure record and nothing else.
sme_map_roles.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `strand` -- the input's `strand`, verbatim; `roles` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id": <a short unique id>, "context": <one or two sentences>, "attributes": [<one short phrase of the proposition>, ...] }`; `relations` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id": <a short unique id, no Role's>, "between": [<two or more Role ids>], "holds": <one sentence> }`; and `higher_order` -- `{ "relates": [<two or more relation ids>], "holds": <one sentence> }`.
sme_map_roles.refusal: a key the record, a Role, a relation or `higher_order` does not declare, or a declared key missing; an id that is empty, repeated, or names nothing; a `strand` that is not the input's; and a Role without `attributes`, refused naming the Role, an `attributes` that is not a list, refused naming the Role, or an entry that is empty, not text or repeated within the Role, refused naming the Role and the index; a `context` carrying `reader`, `you`, `must hold`, `must come to`, `Persona` or `writer` as a word, refused naming the Role and the word; and a relation's `holds` not carrying `{<id>}` for a Role its `between` names, refused naming the relation and the Role, or a `higher_order` `holds` carrying none of the Roles its relations relate. The first refusal is put back into your next round verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial.
sme_map_roles.governing: specs/spec-draft-pipeline/SPEC.md, The Mapper's structure reading; kogaki#1665; kogaki#1720

smp_bind_move.note: The short Trial's `bind` stage (kogaki#1700, kogaki#1719): one model call binds the Move of the Base Paragraph to the structure, declares whether that paragraph tells the proposition's own case or a case apart, and binds the Move of the Inference Paragraph where the case is apart, before any base is named. Under the Mapper's one-retry bound.
smp_bind_move.judgment_point: choose ONE Move of `moves` in the input for the Base Paragraph: a Move whose `segments`, in order, can carry the relations and then the higher-order relation of `structure`, and every entry of whose `takes` the reader in `persona` meets from `persona.prior_knowledge`. Answer its id as `base_move`. Then declare the Base Paragraph's case as `case`: `own` where it tells the proposition's own case, `apart` where it tells a case apart from the proposition's domain. A Move is neutral to the case: choose the case the reader's `persona.prior_knowledge` and the Move's `segments` make tellable, never one read from the Move's `leaves`. Where `case` is `apart`, the reader is owed the case carried onto the subject: choose ONE Move of `moves` for the Inference Paragraph whose `takes` holds an entry of kind `carry`, and answer its id as `inference_move`; where `case` is `own`, answer `inference_move` null. Choose no base domain and no wording: they are named after this call, under the Move you bind and the case you declare.
smp_bind_move.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `base_move` -- one Move id of `moves`; `case` -- `own` or `apart`; and `inference_move` -- one Move id of `moves` under `apart`, null under `own`.
smp_bind_move.refusal: a key the record does not declare, or a declared key missing; a `case` other than `own` or `apart`; a `base_move` or `inference_move` naming no Move of `moves`, refused naming the id; an `inference_move` null where `case` is `apart`, or given where `case` is `own`, refused naming the case; and an `inference_move` whose `takes` holds no `carry`, refused naming the Move. The first refusal is put back into your next round verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial at `bind`.
smp_bind_move.governing: specs/spec-draft-pipeline/SPEC.md, The short Trial; kogaki#1700; kogaki#1719

smp_correspondence.note: The Mapper's grounding, the short Trial's `grounding` stage (kogaki#1700, kogaki#1709, kogaki#1721): one model call per bound Move, the base Move's first, fills that Move's Mapping Table under its Segments; each call is given `case`, the base Move's the one `bind` declared and the inference Move's `own` (kogaki#1719), and the inference call is also given `prior_tables`, the base Move's table. Each answer is validated by `validateCorrespondenceTable`, as each table of the owner's file is (kogaki#1693). Under the Mapper's one-retry bound.
smp_correspondence.judgment_point: name ONE domain the reader in `persona` already holds, from `persona.prior_knowledge`, in which the Roles, the relations and the higher-order relation of `structure` hold as stated and in which the `segments` in the input, the Segments of the Move bound to the paragraph this table serves, can be performed in order. Name the domain in one phrase as `base.domain`. Then name, for EVERY Role of `structure`, in the structure's order, one Correspondence expression as its `expression`: a noun phrase of that domain naming the object that plays the Role, written so that it reads in place of `{<id>}` in each `holds` sentence, where `{<id>}` stands for the Role of that id. Where `case` in the input is `apart`, `base.domain` is a domain apart from the proposition's, and no expression names the proposition's object or an entry of a Role's `attributes`; where `case` is `own`, `base.domain` is the proposition's, and each expression is the proposition's own noun phrase for the Role, its `attributes` included. Where the input carries `prior_tables`, they are the tables of the cases already told, the Base Paragraph's first; where a Segment likens the subject to a case already told, that case is `prior_tables` and its expressions may be named.
smp_correspondence.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `base` -- `{ "domain": <one phrase> }`; and `correspondences` -- one `{ "role": <the Role's id>, "expression": <one noun phrase> }` per Role of `structure`, in the structure's order.
smp_correspondence.refusal: a key the record does not declare; a `base` that is not `{ domain }`, refused naming the key; an `expression` that is not one non-empty text, refused naming `correspondences[<i>].expression`; a `role` naming no Role of `structure`, refused naming the id; and a Role with other than one correspondence, refused naming the Role. The first refusal is put back into your next round verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial at `grounding`.

smp_read_move.note: The Brief-Leg route's `move-reading` stage (kogaki#1830): one model call reads the named Move into its structure before any Segment is read for what it states. Validated by `validateMoveStructure`. Under the Mapper's one-retry bound.
smp_read_move.judgment_point: read the Move in the input, `move`, as a whole: its `description` and all its `segments` in order. Name the Roles the Move needs as `roles`, each with an `id`, a `context` of one or two sentences defining it as a kind of thing, its `attributes` (one short phrase each, or an empty list), and its `source`: `target` for a Role the proposition the Move is used for supplies, `base` for a Role the reader's own domain supplies. Name the relations among those Roles the Move builds as `relations`, each with an `id`, `between` naming the Roles it relates and `holds`, one sentence stating it with each Role written as `{<id>}`; and the relations among relations as `higher_order`, each with an `id`, `relates` naming the relations it relates and `holds`, or an empty list where the Move builds none. Create no Role or relation from one Segment's operation alone: read them over the whole Move first. Only then, as `segments`, record for each Segment in order which of those Roles, relations and higher-order relations it states, as `{ "segment": <its number>, "states": [<ids>] }`; a Segment may state none, and every Role and relation is stated by at least one Segment.
smp_read_move.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `roles` -- a non-empty list of `{ "id", "context", "attributes": [...], "source": "target" | "base" }`; `relations` -- a list of `{ "id", "between": [<Role ids>], "holds" }`; `higher_order` -- a list of `{ "id", "relates": [<relation ids>], "holds" }`; and `segments` -- one `{ "segment": <1, 2, ...>, "states": [<ids>] }` per Segment of `move`, in order.
smp_read_move.refusal: a key the record or an entry does not declare, or a declared key missing; an empty or repeated id; a `source` other than `target` or `base`, refused naming the Role; a relation naming no Role, or a higher-order relation naming no relation, refused naming it; a `segments` list that is not one entry per Segment in order, refused naming the count or the entry; a `states` id naming nothing, refused naming the Segment and the id; and a Role, relation or higher-order relation no Segment states, refused naming it. The first refusal is put back into your next round verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial at `move-reading`.

smp_pair_roles.note: The Brief-Leg route's `pairing` stage (kogaki#1830): one model call pairs the Move's structure with the Leg's. Validated by `validatePairing`; the Harness then writes what is left `unmatched`. Under the Mapper's one-retry bound.
smp_pair_roles.judgment_point: pair the Move's structure in the input, `move_structure`, with the Leg's, `leg_structure`. For EVERY Role of `move_structure` whose `source` is `target`, answer one `{ "move_role": <its id>, "leg_role": <the id of the Leg Role that plays it, or null> }` in `role_pairs`; a Role whose `source` is `base` is not paired. For EVERY relation and higher-order relation of `move_structure`, answer one `{ "move_relation": <its id>, "leg_relation": <the id of the Leg relation or higher-order relation it is, or null> }` in `relation_pairs`. Answer null where the Leg holds nothing that plays the Move's element, and never name a Leg element for it that does not: a null is recorded as unmatched, and nothing fills it. No Leg Role or Leg relation is named by two pairs, and a relation is paired only with a Leg relation that holds the Leg Roles its own Roles are paired with.
smp_pair_roles.input_shape: ONE record AT THE RECORD'S OWN ROOT carrying exactly these keys: `role_pairs` -- one `{ "move_role", "leg_role" }` per `target` Role of `move_structure`; and `relation_pairs` -- one `{ "move_relation", "leg_relation" }` per relation and higher-order relation of `move_structure`; `leg_role` and `leg_relation` are an id of `leg_structure` or null.
smp_pair_roles.refusal: a key the record or a pair does not declare; a missing or repeated pair, refused naming the Move's element; an id naming nothing, refused naming the pair; a Role whose `source` is `base` in `role_pairs`; a Leg Role or Leg relation named by two pairs, refused naming both; and a relation pair where a Role of the Move's relation is paired with a Role the Leg's relation does not hold, refused naming the pair and the Role. A null is not refused. The first refusal is put back into your next round verbatim with your answer; a second ends the Trial at `pairing`.

smp_paired_plan.note: The Brief-Leg route's `waypoints` stage (kogaki#1830): this row's one sentence is appended to the production `paragraph_plan_unit` row's judgment point on that route alone, the production row unchanged; the call is handed `move_structure` and `pairing` beside the row's own inputs.
smp_paired_plan.judgment_point: Where the input carries `move_structure` and `pairing`, a Waypoint written for a Segment uses the Leg Roles paired with the Roles that Segment `states` in `move_structure.segments`, and writes nothing for a Role or relation the `pairing` leaves unmatched.
